scope: Finite exact resource ceilings for worst-case exhaustive planning, deterministic unstructured verified search, and bounded verification under exchangeable defect locations. These are bounded G2 impossibility/tightness results, not a morphology-to-capability G6 predictor.
assumptions: all resource budgets and task families are frozen before protected outcomes
planning is over a full finite b-ary tree with no pruning, transposition merging, heuristic oracle or structure that rules out branches
search is over a finite unstructured candidate class with a perfect membership verifier and no inference or side channel relating unchecked candidates to checked candidates
verification checks distinct obligation coordinates perfectly, defect locations are exchangeable under the registered uniform-r-subset model, and adoption occurs when all inspected coordinates pass
every theorem states an exact zero-error or explicitly distributional boundary and refuses claims outside that boundary
evidence_class: P1 formal theorem family plus P2 exhaustive finite witnesses
strongest_parents: deterministic decision-tree/query complexity for unstructured search
acceptance sampling and the hypergeometric distribution
falsifier: An in-scope finite instance violates a stated bound while its scope guards and resource accounting remain exactly satisfied.

ceilings.quantity: Full b-ary planning tree, exhaustive node-inspection budget R, and guaranteed complete horizon h.
ceilings.theorem: In a full b-ary tree where any uninspected node through depth h may contain the only goal or obligation-changing event, a planner that guarantees complete zero-error coverage through depth h must inspect every node through that depth. The required node count is N(b,h)=h+1 for b=1 and (b^(h+1)-1)/(b-1) for b>1. The bound is tight by breadth-first exhaustive inspection.
ceilings.bound: N(b,h) <= R. For b>1, h <= floor(log_b(R(b-1)+1))-1; for b=1, h <= R-1.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Uninformed tree-search branching-factor complexity / exhaustive search.
assumptions: finite full b-ary tree and integer horizon h>=0
node inspection is the metered planning resource
any node through depth h may be adversarially decisive
no heuristic oracle, pruning certificate, state merging/transposition, or structural dominance rule
guarantee is complete worst-case coverage, not success on one lucky path
ceilings.negative_twin: A binary tree with R=14 cannot guarantee complete depth 3 because depth 3 contains 15 nodes including the root; R=15 is tight.
ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope planner guarantees complete depth h after inspecting fewer than N(b,h) nodes.

ceilings.quantity: N unstructured candidates, one hidden valid candidate, and Q deterministic membership-verifier queries.
ceilings.theorem: If exactly one of N candidates may be valid and validity of one candidate gives no information about any other, every deterministic algorithm that guarantees finding the valid candidate in the worst case requires Q>=N membership queries. With Q<N, an adversary places the unique valid candidate at an unqueried index. The bound is tight by querying all candidates.
ceilings.bound: Worst-case guaranteed verified-solution class size <= Q; complete guarantee over N candidates requires Q>=N.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Deterministic decision-tree/query complexity for unstructured search.
assumptions: finite candidate set with exactly one potentially valid location
validity membership oracle is exact
candidate identities are unstructured and checking one candidate gives no information about another
no generative shortcut, ordering promise, heuristic oracle, side information, or parallel unmetered verification
worst-case zero-error guarantee
ceilings.negative_twin: N=5 candidates with Q=4 queries; whichever four indices are checked, the fifth can be the unique valid candidate.
ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope deterministic search guarantees the unique valid candidate for all placements with Q<N queries.

ceilings.quantity: M obligation coordinates, exactly r defective coordinates chosen uniformly among all r-subsets, and q distinct perfect checks without replacement.
ceilings.theorem: Under exchangeable defect locations and no defect-location side information, any non-anticipating verifier that inspects q distinct coordinates and adopts iff all inspected coordinates pass misses every defect with probability C(M-q,r)/C(M,r), interpreted as zero when M-q<r. This is therefore the exact false-adoption probability for the registered model. In the distribution-free adversarial single-defect model, any q<M leaves an unchecked coordinate on which an invalid candidate can be placed, so zero worst-case false adoption requires q=M.
ceilings.bound: P_FA(q;M,r)=C(M-q,r)/C(M,r). For r=1, P_FA=(M-q)/M. Worst-case adversarial zero-FA requires q=M.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Acceptance sampling / hypergeometric sampling without replacement.
assumptions: finite M obligation coordinates and 1<=r<=M defects
the r-defect set is uniformly distributed over all r-subsets for the probabilistic bound
q distinct checks are chosen without defect-location side information
each checked defect is detected perfectly
candidate is adopted iff no checked coordinate fails
ceilings.negative_twin: M=10, r=1, q=8 has exact false-adoption probability 2/10; full q=10 verification has probability 0.
ceilings.falsifier: Under the registered exchangeable perfect-check model, measured exact enumeration disagrees with C(M-q,r)/C(M,r), or a q<M deterministic verifier guarantees zero false adoption against an adversarial single defect.
